findings.reason: Direction survives but the 43%-vs-80% completion / 48%-vs-72% checkout-reach magnitude is confounded by a live-vs-preview DOMAIN asymmetry, not the theme. meta.jsonl proves OLD ran on live crooksldn.com and reached a WORKING /checkouts/cn/... page, while NEW ran on shopifypreview.com and hit the preview checkout block (F-DN3). The 4 checkout-click-failed personas are a pure preview artifact worth ~13 of the 37 completion points; crediting them lifts NEW buy-now to ~57%. Of 17 cited ids, 3 completed on NEW and 6 also failed on OLD. Durable theme core is ~a third of the gap, driven by F2 (search).
findings.caveat: NEW buy-now is plausibly somewhat worse (verified search break), but 43/80 and 48/72 are not like-for-like: OLD=live (checkout works) vs NEW=preview (checkout blocked + consent overlay). >=13 of 37 points are the preview block alone.

findings.reason: search-opened-mobile.jpg / search-after-typing.jpg show NEW /search reading 'NO RECORDS MATCH THAT QUERY' with no usable input (Staging footer); typing changed nothing; live-checks new_search=no-input-found. old/j2/mobile/step-02-search-suggest.jpg shows OLD's working predictive dropdown. Verified live, correct themes, not true of both. Only nuance: 'abandoned:12' is loose (7 abandon primarily at search). Core functional claim ironclad.

NEW accordion win is real and verbatim-verified (14-day returns, free UK shipping >£20/Tracked24 >£70, UK 1-2/intl 7-14 days). But 'OLD has NO shipping/returns info anywhere (not on PDP)' is overstated: OLD PDP visibly shows '9-16 days delivery UK / 16-21 intl' and a FREE UK SHIPPING banner (old_pdp_bodytext_has shipping_cost:true, returns_days:true).
findings.caveat: Accurate gap: OLD PDP shows delivery timeframes + free-shipping banner but has no findable RETURNS policy and no UI-linked policy pages; NEW surfaces a complete structured policy incl. 14-day returns one tap away. Causal link to 0% completion holds for lookup-support; weaker for research-compare.

findings.reason: Recomputed from 200 theme-labeled verdicts: feels_like OLD brand49/reseller31/template20 -> NEW brand81/template19/reseller0 (exact); price OLD mid98 -> NEW premium44/mid45 (exact); brand_recall 'crooksldn' OLD=0 vs NEW=15 (finding's 11 is conservative). Preview-artifact attack fails: shift is driven by concept words (case-file 27, terminal 7), and OLD's header renders the wordmark yet scored 0 recall while NEW scored 15. Identical prices, so premium-vs-mid is a pure perception shift.

collection-all-desktop.jpg (Staging) shows NEW /collections/all with only category tabs, zero sort/filter (live-checks new_collection_controls=[]). old/j4/desktop shows OLD's Availability filter + Sort ('open-filter-sort ok:true'). Correct themes, theme-rendered UI, not true of both.

Structural claim verified: OLD header shows a USD/GBP selector (old_currency_ui), NEW has none (new_currency_ui=[]). But impact is double-counted: the £/$ clash is a SHARED artifact (F-SHARED1 NEW43/OLD42); F6's count 43 equals the shared confusion population re-attributed to the switcher removal.
findings.caveat: Removed selector is a genuine NEW regression, but incremental impact over the shared £/$ confusion is small and not isolated; rely on the 14 listed ids, not '43 affected'.

findings.reason: Popup real but mis-cited and over-counted. Cited step-02-zoom-pdp-200pct.jpg shows the COOKIE CONSENT modal, not the popup. Real CRACK THE CUFFS modal is in step-01-zoom-home-200pct.jpg and j6/desktop footer capture — desktop only; did not reproduce on mobile in 20s. Only ~20 personas reference CRACK (17 desktop/3 mobile); the other ~25 'popup' mentions are cookie-consent reactions. Only 7 of 14 listed ids mention CRACK.
findings.caveat: Real NEW element harming popup-averse desktop shoppers, but '35 personas' conflates consent reactions with the discount popup; defensible count ~20, desktop-predominant, non-reproducing on mobile.

findings.reason: Core verified: NEW desktop header omits ACCOUNT (in MENU drawer); OLD shows a persistent person icon. But framed as DESKTOP while 8 of 14 listed ids are MOBILE, and 7 of those didn't abandon at account. Both themes reach the same working login (F-SHARED2).
findings.caveat: Real desktop-header regression, but affected set padded with mobile personas; '19 affected' overstates it — clean impact is the few desktop returning personas.

NEW-specific (OLD shows plain price). ~30 verdicts reference FILED vs claimed 37 — modest overcount, mechanism intact.

Reproduces from raw verdicts: recall maze=9, broken-search=6, popup=4; feels_like template=19%; ~11 'unknowable/no-price' price guesses. NEW-specific: OLD's cluster is generic-but-legible (plain/basic/grey/empty), a different failure mode. Honest flip side of F4.
